title: Malware Infects Android-Based Automotive Head Unit Firmware
summary: Kaspersky researchers discovered a new multi-stage Android malware targeting automotive head units, spreading via built-in firmware updaters. The malware, attributed to the MoYu Group (linked to the BADBOX botnet), operates as a clicker for ad fraud and a reverse proxy for botnet recruitment. The infection chain exploits a legitimate system app (TWCore) to deliver malicious payloads in three stages: a dropper (JarService), a loader, and a final payload (zhima module) for ad fraud or proxy functionality. This marks the first documented case of malware specifically designed for car head units.
key_points: First documented case of malware targeting Android-based automotive head units.
Malware spreads via compromised firmware updaters in head units, exploiting a legitimate system app (TWCore) with an `installNotExists` flag.
Three-stage infection chain: JarService dropper → loader → clicker/reverse proxy (zhima module).
Primary purposes: ad fraud (clicker) and recruitment into a proxy botnet.
Attributed to the MoYu Group, linked to the BADBOX botnet.
Malware uses encrypted payloads, dynamic C2 communication, and reflection-based execution to evade detection.
Commands include HTTP requests, clipboard manipulation, WebView exploitation, and arbitrary code execution.
Vendor (DoFun) was notified and has since patched the security issues.
